items.title: How fast does a route-at-a-time migration actually finish?
items.description: A 20-route legacy system migrates one small, reversible bet at a time. Drag how many routes the team migrates per week to see how many weeks until every route is on the new system — and remember the big-bang alternative delivers zero customer value until month 14 (~60 weeks) no matter what.
items.compute: const totalRoutes = 20; const weeksToFullMigration = Math.ceil(totalRoutes / params.routesPerWeek); return { weeksToFullMigration };

outputs.label: Weeks until every route is migrated

items.title: How many requests does a bad rollout percentage actually expose?
items.description: GET /products sees about 50,000 requests a day. Drag the routing table's rollout percentage for the new system to see how many of today's requests would hit a bug on it — this is exactly the number the facade shrinks to zero the moment you flip that one entry back to "legacy".
items.compute: const dailyRequests = 50000; const affectedRequests = Math.round(dailyRequests * (params.rolloutPercent / 100)); return { affectedRequests };

outputs.label: Requests per day hitting the new system

items.title: How much shadow traffic does it take to actually catch a rare bug?
items.description: A 100% match rate over two weeks only proves the new system agrees with the old one on the traffic that occurred. For a bug that only shows up on roughly 1 in N requests (at 50,000 requests/day), drag the shadow window and the bug's rarity to see the real odds of it surfacing at all before you flip the route to 100%.

params.name: bugFrequency
params.label: Bug shows up 1 in every N requests

items.compute: const dailyTraffic = 50000; const sampledRequests = dailyTraffic * params.shadowDays; const survivalProbability = Math.pow(1 - 1 / params.bugFrequency, sampledRequests); const detectionChancePercent = Math.round((1 - survivalProbability) * 1000) / 10; return { detectionChancePercent };

outputs.label: Chance the shadow window catches the bug
